clue.text: Superior agent bringing government security

parts.note: premium as an adjective means superior or top quality
James Bond, the fictional secret agent

explanation.surface: A top spy delivers state security, perhaps a defence briefing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Security' here is the financial sense: a Premium Bond is a British savings bond issued by the government, paying prizes by lottery instead of interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Premium Bonds are savings certificates backed by the UK Treasury, a kind of financial instrument issued by the state.

clue.text: Stars helping to create something groundbreaking

parts.note: the Plough is the British name for the star pattern known in America as the Big Dipper
a helping is a portion or share

explanation.surface: Celebrities lending a hand to produce an innovative project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groundbreaking' sounds like innovative, but read literally it is a blade that cuts the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: The cutting blade of a farm plough literally slices open the earth as it is drawn through a field.

clue.text: European clubs wearing black kick out

indicators.note: something wearing an item has it on, wrapped around it, so one letter sits inside the colour word

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black

explanation.surface: Continental football clubs in black strips expelling someone, or a referee sending players off.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel or throw someone out of a place is to force their removal, the same as booting them out.

clue.text: One in a state needing aid on a horse, desperately

indicators.note: acting desperately means acting wildly and without order, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: Someone in a bad way pleading for help to get onto a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in a state' reads like someone distressed; it means a resident of one of the US states, Idaho.
explanation.definitionFit: An Idahoan is a resident of Idaho, a western American state, so literally an inhabitant of one of the fifty.

clue.text: Within minutes, trunk road's put out of action

indicators.note: within means inside, so the road's letters sit between the two time units

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for minute, so two of them
the A1 is Britain's longest trunk road, read as the letters A and I

explanation.surface: A main road closed within minutes, perhaps after an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 runs from London to Edinburgh; in crosswords the digit 1 is often read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To maim is to injure badly enough to disable, leaving a person or limb unable to function.

clue.text: Tempt with onion crackers, supremely strong

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the preceding words go mad and rearrange

explanation.surface: Trying to lure someone with onion-flavoured biscuits that pack a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackers' looks like biscuits to eat with onion; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnipotent means all-powerful, having unlimited might, which is strength taken to its highest degree.

clue.text: Unravelling vital code saved Vatican official

indicators.note: unravelling pulls threads apart and loose, so the letters come undone and are rewoven

explanation.surface: A codebreaker cracking a cipher rescues a papal official, like a Dan Brown thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devil's Advocate was the Church lawyer appointed to argue against canonising a candidate for sainthood.

clue.text: Two police informers that could feed many behind bars

definitions.text: that could feed many behind bars

parts.note: a canary sings, so it is slang for an informer
grass is British slang for an informer

explanation.surface: Two prison snitches whose tips might fill the cells with inmates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind bars' suggests prisoners; the bars are those of a birdcage, and canary grass seed is bird food.
explanation.definitionFit: Canary grass is grown for birdseed, which feeds caged songbirds kept in households.

clue.text: GPs might welcome these queries regularly during visits

indicators.note: during means in the course of something, so these letters sit inside another word

parts.note: a doctor's house calls are visits

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Doctors pleased by patients' questions on home visits.
explanation.walkthrough: A cure-all is a panacea, a remedy for every ailment; a busy GP would happily accept one.
explanation.definitionFit: Family doctors would love universal remedies that heal every complaint, making the panacea welcome in surgery.

clue.text: Ring through snout a form of restraint

indicators.note: a ring put through a snout sits inside it, so one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: a snout is an animal's nose

explanation.surface: A ring through a bull's nose, used to lead and control it.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop of rope tightened around the neck or limb holds and confines the person or creature caught.

clue.text: Beginnings of weak energy seen in puniest creatures

indicators.note: seen in places these letters inside the other word

parts.note: runts are the smallest of a litter

explanation.surface: The smallest animals in a litter show little vigour at birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudiments are the basic first principles of a subject, the elementary starting points of learning.

clue.text: Records in diary reflected evangelist's message

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the whole is read backwards
in places one word within the other

parts.note: a log is a daily record

explanation.surface: A preacher's diary entries mirrored in his sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: The gospel is the Christian good news preached by evangelists, the message of the New Testament writers.

clue.text: Achievement of a parent full of energy engaged in short flight

indicators.note: full of means holding something inside
short means cut off, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to be in on something is to be engaged in it

explanation.surface: A proud parent, buzzing with energy, joins a brief plane trip as a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' is not air travel but running away.
explanation.definitionFit: A feather in one's cap is an idiom for an accomplishment to be proud of, from plumes worn as honours.

clue.text: Homeless aristo given a hearing forthwith

indicators.note: giving something a hearing means listening to it, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: a homeless person lives on the street; toff is British slang for an upper-class person

explanation.surface: A down-and-out nobleman gets his case heard at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight off means immediately, without delay, the same as at once or forthwith.

clue.text: Past master following surgeon's work, an invasive procedure

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the second part is placed later

parts.note: over means finished, in the past

explanation.surface: An old hand follows a surgeon's operation, which is invasive surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invasive procedure' sounds medical; it was the codename for the 1944 Allied invasion of Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: The D-Day landings of 1944 were codenamed this, a military assault and seaborne invasion of occupied France.

clue.text: Coat in two sizes gaining appreciation

indicators.note: gaining means adding something on, here at the end

parts.note: S and M, small and medium clothing sizes
an ear for music is an appreciation of it

explanation.surface: A coat stocked in two sizes is gaining approval with shoppers.
explanation.definitionFit: To smear is to spread something thickly across a surface, as one would coat it.

clue.text: Agrees fares, as passenger does

definitions.meaning: first meaning: is friendly or gets along with someone
second meaning: progresses, and also boards a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone accepts the ticket prices, as a bus traveller does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fares' looks like ticket prices; it is the verb, as in 'how is he faring', and the passenger who boards supplies a third sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers getting along with someone, making progress, and stepping aboard a train or bus.

clue.text: What's lost by guru bottling medicine?

indicators.note: bottling something holds it inside

parts.note: a sage is a wise teacher
a pill is a dose of medicine

explanation.surface: A guru keeping medicine in a bottle wonders what goes missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Spillage is the amount of liquid that escapes or is wasted when something overflows or tips over.

clue.text: Concert stars from Emirates, heading off abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so the letters are scattered
heading off removes the head, the first letter

explanation.surface: Star performers fly off abroad on the Emirates airline.
explanation.walkthrough: Emirates looks like the airline carrying musicians abroad; both words are instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestri is the Italian plural of maestro, used for eminent conductors and virtuoso musicians.

clue.text: Convict's singular ambition reduced

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A prisoner's one great aspiration has been cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convict' is the verb here: in Britain a judge sends a criminal down, to prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To send down is British slang for sentencing someone to jail after a guilty verdict.

clue.text: I invested in second family home minimally well covered

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it

parts.note: a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Someone puts money into a holiday house that is barely insured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well covered' sounds like insurance; it means plump, so the least well covered is the thinnest.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well covered is a jokey way of saying plump, so having the least flesh means being thinnest.

clue.text: Having started outside, a lion is somehow confined

indicators.note: placed outside means wrapping around the other letters

parts.note: to institute is to start something

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lion that began life in the wild ends up shut in a zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has lived long in a hospital or prison and is shaped by it, or simply committed to such a place.

clue.text: Claiming everyone died escaping from border

indicators.note: escaping from something means getting out of it, so a letter leaves

explanation.surface: Asserting that everyone perished fleeing across a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert something without proof, so alleging is making a claim.

clue.text: Drink that's right during interval? Pop

indicators.note: during means in the middle of a period, so this letter goes inside

parts.note: pop and pa are both informal words for father

explanation.surface: Asking whether a fizzy drink is the right thing for the theatre interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like soda; it is Dad.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappa is an Italian brandy distilled from grape skins and pips left after winemaking, a strong alcoholic spirit.

clue.text: College coach not head of athletics

indicators.note: not means without, so the named head letter is removed

explanation.surface: A college sports coach who isn't in charge of athletics.
explanation.walkthrough: A tech is short for a technical college in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tech is the informal British short form for a technical college, an institution of further education.

clue.text: On cruise ship, disheartened, drink more stout

indicators.note: disheartened is read as losing its heart, the middle letter
in a down clue, on means placed above, so the drink sits on top

parts.note: a liner is a passenger ship

explanation.surface: A dispirited passenger on a cruise drinks more Guinness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like the dark beer, chiming with the drink; here it means fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Portly means stout or plump, so the comparative describes someone who is fatter or more rotund.

clue.text: Tea service, third of plates going west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means travelling right to left, backwards
third of picks the letter in third position

explanation.surface: A tea service with some plates being sent west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea service' reads as one item of crockery, but the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a strong black tea grown in the north-eastern Indian state of the same name.

clue.text: Dress badly, something actor should never do, we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so the sound matters

parts.note: an actor must not forget a piece of dialogue

explanation.surface: Wearing the wrong clothes is a sin for any actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' is the military sense, to line troops up straight; dressing badly leaves the rank crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: In drill, to dress ranks is to bring soldiers into straight line, so putting them out of line is the opposite.

clue.text: Turn against one splitting party from the start

indicators.note: splitting something means going into its middle and dividing it
to turn round is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: Someone who turned against a party member splitting it right from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: De novo is Latin for anew, starting again from the beginning, as in a fresh trial.

clue.text: Jazz musician's men briefly recalled playing piece

briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

a domino is a tile used in a game

explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing piece' looks like a tune; it is a game tile.

clue.text: Junior in service reserved bread for nursery breakfast?

parts.note: private means reserved, kept to oneself
soldiers are British for thin strips of toast dipped into boiled eggs, a child's breakfast

explanation.surface: A young servant shyly set aside bread for the children's breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' sounds like domestic service; it is the armed services, where the lowest rank is a private.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest rank in the army is the ordinary enlisted man, the most junior serving member.

clue.text: Issue rebounding sound when phone card's installed

indicators.note: rebounding means bouncing back, so the result is read backwards
something installed is fitted inside

parts.note: the SIM card in a mobile phone

explanation.surface: A problem with echoing noise once a phone's SIM card is fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a problem; here it means a discharge.
explanation.definitionFit: An emission is something sent out or discharged, as an issue is an outflow, of gas, fluid or light.

clue.text: Get the better of twenty fielders not performing well

parts.note: point is a cricket fielding position square of the batsman on the off side

explanation.surface: Beating a team of twenty fielders who are having an off day.
explanation.walkthrough: Point is a cricket fielding position; a cricket team fields eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: To score points off someone is to outdo them in argument, winning small victories over them.

clue.text: Disorganised at home, like philanthropist

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
Henry Tate, the sugar magnate who founded London's Tate Gallery

explanation.surface: A wealthy benefactor living in a mess at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like philanthropist' seems to describe the person; it splits into a short word and a famous name.

clue.text: A fixed silver mounting for gemstones

clue.text: Large whisky, say in local producing bad language

parts.note: a local is a native of a place

explanation.surface: A large Scotch ordered in the pub leads to swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' and 'bad language' suggest a British pub and swearing; the bad language is a grammatical fault.

clue.text: Inspector's benevolence, almost total, is shocking

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: DI is Detective Inspector, plus the s

explanation.surface: A police inspector's near-total kindness surprisingly shocks people.

clue.text: Pallid quality a bad sign in clarets, perhaps season's first

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter

clue.text: Public official, speech back to front, to support queen

indicators.note: the back letter is moved round to the front

explanation.surface: A civic official's speech is muddled, but he still backs the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword-bearer is a civic officer who carries the ceremonial sword before a mayor or monarch.

clue.text: The unmissable "Sparkling sequin" by prolific author

parts.note: Anonymous has written more works than anyone

explanation.definitionFit: Sine qua non is Latin for an essential condition, literally without which nothing, so something indispensable.

clue.text: Missile launchers stolen on board with prior support from medic

parts.note: the hare is a fast runner

explanation.definitionFit: Being strict or particular means insisting on exact standards and not tolerating sloppiness.

clue.text: American word for depot?

parts.note: read as 'in US', in the United States

explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a dictionary question about American usage; it is read as a word plus 'in US'.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is the end station or depot of a bus or rail line, where vehicles stop and turn round.

clue.text: Beguiled consultant's discipline criticised

parts.note: ear, nose and throat, a hospital speciality
rapped as in rapped over the knuckles

explanation.surface: A charmed hospital consultant has his speciality slammed.

clue.text: Scots town has equipment for stylist wanting all-round trim

clue.text: Elevated accountant given exclusive housing as compensation

clue.text: Pizza dish from region east of Golden State

explanation.definitionFit: Cumulous describes heaped, piled-up formations, the adjective for the fluffy cumulus type seen in the sky.

clue.text: Socialist bound by firm principles

clue.text: Several hands needed for this dental work

clue.text: Civet spied in grass, often retreating

clue.text: "Loos" misread in translation as more exclusive facilities?

clue.text: Chance inaccuracy from tabloid (E for I) backing organised party

the Daily Mirror, a British tabloid newspaper
